answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Speech to the Team after the Semi-final

Good evening, friends and Coach Sir,

I know that every one of us is hurting today. We came so close to the final of the First Inter School Football Competition, and we lost to the team that went on to win the cup. It is all right to feel disappointed. It shows how much we cared. But I have called you together not to look back in sadness, but to look forward with hope.

First, let us be honest about where we fell short. Our passing in the middle of the field was not accurate enough, and we lost the ball too often under pressure. In the second half we were tired, which tells me our stamina needs work. We also missed two easy chances in front of goal. And at the corner that gave them their winning goal, our marking was loose.

Now let us look at the positives, because there are many. We were the only team that scored twice against the champions. Our defence kept three clean sheets on the way to the semi-final. Our goalkeeper made some brilliant saves, and our younger players showed that they are ready for big matches. Most of all, we never gave up. Even when we were behind, we kept fighting till the final whistle. That spirit cannot be taught; we already have it.

So here is my plan for the future. From next week, we will train an extra half hour every morning to build stamina. Twice a week we will practise short, quick passing drills and shooting in front of goal. Our defenders will practise set pieces with Coach Sir. We will also watch videos of our matches to learn from our mistakes. And we will play friendly matches against stronger teams, because we grow only by facing the best.

Friends, one defeat does not define us. Champions are not those who never fall, but those who rise every time they fall. Next year, let us return to this competition stronger, fitter and more united, and bring the trophy home to our school.

Thank you.

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.finalAnswer: The writer's Research Methodology teacher; after each class he tore up his class notes and threw them in the waste paper basket, so that he would not repeat today's knowledge tomorrow and put himself and the class to sleep.
answers.solution: The strange habit belongs to one of the writer's teachers, who taught Research Methodology. After each class, he would tear off his class notes and throw them into the waste paper basket. He did this because if he kept the notes, he would tend to repeat the same things in the next class, and that would put him and the whole class to sleep. He wanted to teach what he learnt afresh each day.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: What the teacher would learn the next day (fresh, new learning).
answers.solution:
What the teacher would learn the next day, that is, new and fresh learning, would keep him as well as his class awake.
(The question says 'writer and his students', but in the passage it is the teacher and his class who would be kept awake.)

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: A learned man is stuck with old, past knowledge and stops growing; a man of learning is curious about the present and keeps learning, full of life.
answers.solution: A learned man is someone who is tied to the knowledge of the past. He thinks he knows everything, so he has stopped growing, like an old tree bent under its dead wood. A man of learning, on the other hand, is curious about the present and keeps asking questions. He is lively and eager to learn, like a fresh green twig coming out of the soil after the rains.

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: Because he has all the answers and no room in his head for new questions or discoveries, so he only repeats old knowledge and makes learning dull.
answers.solution: A learned man thinks he has all the answers and leaves no room in his head for new questions or discoveries. He keeps repeating old, dead knowledge, which makes learning dull and lifeless. So he can put not just a class but a whole generation to sleep.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: The heart, the inner core of our being, where our attention is deepest; we point to it when we say 'I'.
answers.solution: The centre of awareness is the heart, the inner core of a person, where our attention is deepest. It is not the biological heart. When a person speaks of himself as 'I', he points his finger towards his heart, which by Nature's design is the centre of his awareness. 'Learning by heart' means taking our attention deep into this centre.

answers.label: Q.2(f)
answers.finalAnswer: To give up its secrets, if we only know how to knock (how to give it the necessary blow).
answers.solution: According to Swami Vivekananda, the world is ready to give up its secrets, if only we know how to knock, that is, how to give it the necessary blow.

answers.label: Q.2(g)
answers.finalAnswer: Concentration gives strength and force to our effort; the more concentrated the mind, the more power it brings to one point.
answers.solution: Concentration gives strength and force to the 'blow' with which we knock at the world's secrets. The more concentrated the mind is, the more power it can bring to bear on one point. So concentration is the key to all learning and discovery.

answers.label: Q.2(h)
answers.finalAnswer: The more concentrated the mind is, the more power is brought to bear on one point.
answers.solution: The secret is the power of concentration: 'The more concentrated it (the mind) is, the more power is brought to bear on one point; that is the secret.' There is no limit to the power of the human mind when it is concentrated.

answers.label: Q.3(a)
answers.finalAnswer: Because old age should be full of the peace that comes from experience and the ripe fulfilment and completeness of a life lived bravely and honestly.
answers.solution: The poet feels it must be lovely to be old because old age should bring the peace that comes from experience. After a life lived bravely (undaunted), without bitterness and without accepting lies, an old person should feel ripe fulfilment and complete satisfaction, and should be soothing and rich like a ripe, sweet-smelling apple.

answers.label: Q.3(b)
answers.finalAnswer: Simile
answers.solution: Simile. Old people are compared to yellowing leaves using the word 'like'.

answers.label: Q.3(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Facing all the ups and downs, hardships and difficulties of life bravely.
answers.solution: 'Facing all weathers' means going through all kinds of situations in life, good and bad, its joys, sorrows, hardships and difficulties, and facing them bravely. The young man admires his father for having lived such a full life.

answers.label: Q.3(d)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) war (unrest); (ii) foul-smelling (stinking); (iii) rejected
answers.solution:
(i) peace: war (or unrest, conflict)
(ii) fragrant: foul-smelling (or stinking)
(iii) accepted: rejected

answers.label: Q.3(e)
answers.finalAnswer: Fearless; not discouraged by difficulty or danger.
answers.solution: 'Undaunted' means fearless, not discouraged or frightened by difficulties or danger. A life lived undaunted is one lived with courage.

answers.label: Q.3(f)
answers.finalAnswer: Beautiful Old Age
answers.solution: A suitable title is 'Beautiful Old Age' (or 'The Beauty of Growing Old'), because the poem describes how lovely, peaceful and fulfilling old age ought to be.

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Topics chosen: (a) and (c).

(a) A rotten apple spoils the barrel
If one apple in a barrel starts to rot, the rot soon spreads to all the others. In the same way, one bad person in a group can spoil everyone around him. In a class, a single student who cheats, bullies or wastes time can lead others to copy him. A team with one selfish player loses its unity. This is why we must choose our friends carefully and avoid bad company. Teachers and leaders, too, must correct a bad influence early, before it spreads. Good habits can spread just as fast, so each of us should try to be a good apple.

(c) Man proposes, God disposes
This proverb means that we can make plans, but the final result is not always in our hands. A farmer may work hard and sow his seeds, but an untimely flood can destroy his crop. A student may prepare well for a match, but an injury can keep him out of it. This does not mean we should stop planning or working. It teaches us to do our best, accept what we cannot control, and not lose heart when things go wrong. Such an attitude keeps us humble in success and calm in failure, and helps us try again.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
From: rohan.sharma@email.com
To: priya.sharma@email.com
Date: 25 June 2021
Subject: What I learnt at summer camp

Dear Priya,

I am back from my ten-day summer camp in Mussoorie and I have so much to tell you! Every morning at six, our instructor made us run, stretch and do yoga. On the first two days I felt tired and sleepy, but by the end of the week I was full of energy. I could climb the hill trail without stopping, I slept better and I felt more cheerful all day. I have now learnt that daily exercise keeps both the body and the mind fit. Please start with a short walk every morning, and we can jog together when I come home.

Thanks and Regards,
Rohan

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
The Last Train Home

"We have plenty of time," said my elder brother Aman, looking at his watch. "The train to Dehradun leaves at six. It is only half past four."

We had spent the whole day at the Delhi book fair, and our bags were heavy with new books. Aman wanted one more plate of chole bhature before we left, so we sat down at a small stall outside the fair. The food took twenty minutes to arrive. By the time we finished, it was already five o'clock.

We walked to the road to find an auto-rickshaw. The first driver asked for too much money, and Aman argued with him. The second one refused to go to the station at all. At last we got one, but soon we were stuck in a huge traffic jam. Cars, buses and scooters stood still in every direction, and horns blared all around us.

"Don't worry," Aman said, though he was no longer smiling.

The minutes ticked by. Quarter past five. Half past five. The auto crept forward a few metres at a time. I kept looking at the clock on my phone, and my heart beat faster with every minute. At twenty to six, the driver turned to us and said that there had been an accident on the flyover ahead and the road was completely blocked.

We jumped out and started running with our heavy bags, weaving between the cars. The station was still two kilometres away. My legs ached and my lungs burned. When we finally saw the station tower in the distance, its big clock showed five minutes to six.

Aman stopped, bent over and gasped for breath. He looked at me and shook his head. In that moment we both knew that we were never going to make it.

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Theme chosen: (a) Exam

The Exam

The exam is near, the clock ticks fast,
I wish the holidays could last.
My books lie open, my pencils are sharp,
My heart is beating like a harp.
I read each chapter, line by line,
And hope the questions will be fine.
I will not worry, I will not fear,
For I have worked hard all the year.
When the bell rings and the paper is done,
I will smile and say the battle is won!

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: missing 'with', preposition, between 'happy' and 'us'; hardly -> hard, adverb; wisely -> wisdom, noun; missing 'them', pronoun, between 'Let' and 'do'; do -> don't, verb (auxiliary); jump -> step, noun; missing 'and', conjunction, between 'Ramesh' and 'Renu'; Alas -> Hurrah, interjection; missing 'much', adjective, between 'How' and 'money'; gets -> get, verb
answers.solution:
(a) Missing word: with. Part of speech: preposition. Location: between 'happy' and 'us'. (He is very happy with us.)
(b) Incorrect word: hardly. Correct word: hard. Part of speech: adverb. ('Hardly' means 'almost not'.)
(c) Incorrect word: wisely. Correct word: wisdom. Part of speech: noun. (It must match the noun 'patience'.)
(d) Missing word: them. Part of speech: pronoun. Location: between 'Let' and 'do'. (Let them do whatever they want.)
(e) Incorrect word: do. Correct word: don't. Part of speech: verb (auxiliary). A positive statement takes a negative question tag: 'They know about your plans, don't they?'
(f) Incorrect word: jump. Correct word: step. Part of speech: noun. (The proverb is 'The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.')
(g) Missing word: and. Part of speech: conjunction. Location: between 'Ramesh' and 'Renu'.
(h) Incorrect word: Alas. Correct word: Hurrah. Part of speech: interjection. ('Alas' expresses sorrow; winning calls for joy.)
(i) Missing word: much. Part of speech: adjective. Location: between 'How' and 'money'. (How much money do you want?)
(j) Incorrect word: gets (the second one). Correct word: get. Part of speech: verb. 'The tough' means tough people, so the verb is plural: 'When the going gets tough, the tough get going.'

answers.label: Q.9
answers.finalAnswer: in the pink of health; the white feather; saw red; the nod; as black as he is painted; pulled off; took to; paid off; came round; acts upon
answers.solution:
(a) He is now in the pink of health. (in the pink = in very good health)
(b) Vikram never showed the white feather in his life. (show the white feather = act like a coward)
(c) The teacher saw red when the naughty boy disturbed others in the class. (see red = become very angry)
(d) If we request him, he will definitely give us the nod. (give the nod = give permission)
(e) He is not as black as he is painted. (not as black as one is painted = not as bad as people say)
(f) The underdog pulled off a stunning victory. (pull off = achieve something difficult)
(g) The actor took to drinking when his movies did not do well. (take to = start a habit)
(h) Dhoni's plan to deceive the batsman paid off. (pay off = succeed)
(i) Very soon he came round. (come round = regain consciousness; 'came to' is also correct)
(j) His parents love him because he always acts upon their advice. (act upon / act on = follow)

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: He is better than most other athletes in the country.; She said that it was time they left the class.; Who is not a fan of Neeraj Chopra?; No sooner did he throw the javelin than he started celebrating.; Why was the house located in the village renovated by his people?; We all saw your bravery.; Despite being given less time to study, he came first in the exam.; The boys said, "Let us go and swim in the river."; The girl was too happy on her birthday to think of her exams.; The boy who is wearing a jacket knows where the sweets have been kept.
answers.solution:
(a) He is better than most other athletes in the country.
(b) She said that it was time they left the class. ('It is time' + past subjunctive keeps 'left'; only the reporting changes.)
(c) Who is not a fan of Neeraj Chopra?
(d) No sooner did he throw the javelin than he started celebrating.
(e) Why was the house located in the village renovated by his people?
(f) We all saw your bravery.
(g) Despite being given less time to study, he came first in the exam.
(h) The boys said, "Let us go and swim in the river."
(i) The girl was too happy on her birthday to think of her exams.
(j) The boy who is wearing a jacket knows where the sweets have been kept.
(In (d) the stem misspells 'javelin' as 'javeline'. In (d) the sentence has no 'not', so the 'negative' form expected is the 'No sooner ... than' pattern; 'He had hardly thrown the javelin when he started celebrating' is also accepted.)

answers.label: Q.11
answers.finalAnswer: (i) Isolate; (iv) Straight forward; (iii) Oppose; (i) Fresh; (iii) Hidden
answers.solution:
(a) Integrate (combine into a whole): antonym (i) Isolate.
Sentence: The sick child was isolated from the others so that the infection would not spread.
(b) Enigmatic (mysterious, hard to understand): antonym (iv) Straightforward.
Sentence: Our coach gave us a straightforward plan that everyone understood.
(c) Concur (agree): antonym (iii) Oppose.
Sentence: Many villagers opposed the plan to cut down the old banyan tree.
(d) Putrid (rotten): antonym (i) Fresh.
Sentence: My mother buys fresh vegetables from the market every morning.
(e) Explicit (stated clearly): antonym (iii) Hidden.
Sentence: The treasure was hidden under the floor of the old house.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.finalAnswer: nation; rational; relation; oriental; retain; talent; linen; intern; train; alien
answers.solution:
INTERNATIONAL has the letters I (2), N (3), T (2), E (1), R (1), A (2), O (1), L (1).
Ten words of five or more letters:
1. NATION
2. RATIONAL
3. RELATION
4. ORIENTAL
5. RETAIN
6. TALENT
7. LINEN
8. INTERN
9. TRAIN
10. ALIEN
Each word uses no letter more often than it appears in INTERNATIONAL (for example RATIONAL uses A twice, and INTERNATIONAL has two A's). Other correct words include LATER, TOTAL, LATTER, NATAL and TENOR.

answers.label: Q.13
answers.finalAnswer: with -> in; too -> very; Beside -> Besides; in -> at; must -> should
answers.solution:
(a) Error: with. Correction: in. (His uncle deals in rice. 'Deal in' means trade in goods.)
(b) Error: too. Correction: very. ('Too' means 'more than needed'; here we simply mean 'very rich'.)
(c) Error: Beside. Correction: Besides. ('Besides' means 'in addition to'; 'beside' means 'next to'.)
(d) Error: in. Correction: at. (We say 'good at' something.)
(e) Error: must. Correction: should. ('Lest' is followed by 'should'.)

answers.label: Q.14
answers.finalAnswer: United we stand, divided we fall; One rotten apple spoils the whole barrel; Strike while the iron is hot; Rome was not built in a day; Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown
answers.solution:
(a) United we stand, divided we fall.
(b) One rotten apple spoils the whole barrel. ('Evil company corrupts good manners' is also correct.)
(c) Strike while the iron is hot. ('Make hay while the sun shines' is also correct.)
(d) Rome was not built in a day.
(e) Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
